posts.content_md:
Hi Dcg Friends, JohnFP, David, Tony and Joe

I have been reading a lot of the old post from John and David. And recalling some of the things I learned From Dinesh. I have a lot of questions and some conclusions on what ive read.

First I did get a review back from the policeman wife and there was a lot of excitement over the hologram of the badge. So it does look like this is in the works but I also what to work on making the product more versatile.

I have many Questions but I will start with this one

There seems to be a contrast difference between silver and Dcg. This is so hard to explain some of you know I come from a photography background so I will use some of those terms to explain. Its seems like dcg is a lot like working with slide film (in contrast), and silver is like working with negatives. In slide film you had 3 Fstops to work with one over and two under. By Fstops I mean units of light like f16 f11 f8 each fstop is twice as much light. So if I wanted to shoot a picture on slide film I would shoot right in the middle of the exposer of the need light and I would get the light one fstop over and one under. So slides always had to be shot with this in mind because of the narrow contrast range. Working with dcg for some time here with the help of my friends JohnFP, David and Dinesh each one has given me a better understanding as I read their post(side note), Its seems that dcg also display this characteristics. As silver has a much more of a wide contrast range. Maybe 7 to 9 Fstop, maybe this is why they don’t use dcg as trans masters H1?

Ok let me continue my thought here... the recording of the contrast of dark and light fringes determine the brightness level of the replay of that wave front. and the lowest point of the light fringes recorded determine the contrast curve of the replay of that wave front... so the more degrees of value (brightness) recorded in the holographic medium the more degrees of midd tones in the reconstruction of that wave front will be seen. Controlling the curve of the recording of this wave front is in my understanding just like the zone system in photography. Weather is the medium or the development or the ratio of reference/object wave used to control it. In controlling this variables will determine 1 brightness 2 contrast (high and low tones) in the final image. Some mediums have different contrast ranges that they can record in the medium.

The Zone System is a photographic technique for determining optimal film exposure and development, formulated by Ansel Adams and Fred Archer in 1941. The Zone System provides photographers with a systematic method of precisely defining the relationship between the way they visualize the photographic subject and the final results, this was taken from Wiki
